entries.description: The world-ash joining Asguard and Mannguard, whose fall closes the age.
entries.note: _heims_ "world's" + _ask_ "ash" — the World-Ash
entries.prose: Heimsask is the world-ash of Asguardian cosmology, rooted in Asguard and crowned over Mannguard, holding the gods’ world and the living world in one growth. The tradition ties their fate to the tree: while it stands, both worlds stand, and when it burns, both burn with it. The skalds name Aldarlok the Fall of the Ash because its falling closes the age. Details beyond that shared account, including the number of its roots, remain matters on which rune-priests and skalds disagree.

entries.description: The honored dead gathered into the gods’ halls to train for Aldarlok.
entries.note: _val-_ + _drengr_ "warrior" (the Compact's "drengr without a hall")
entries.prose: Valdrengir names the honored dead gathered into the defending gods’ halls to wait and train for Aldarlok. The Asguardian account includes fallen warriors, oath-keepers who die keeping their word, mothers who die in childbirth, and craftsmen who fall defending their work. Their principal destinations are Ódvarshöll in Valsal and Sólrúnshöll on Sólvangr. In Valsal, the warriors arm and fight each day, recover their wounds by evening, and feast at the hall. The standard telling musters the honored dead on Vígvöll beside the defending gods for a war they know is lost; their willingness to gather expresses the faith’s virtue of defiance.

entries.prose: Vígvöll is the plain where the defending gods and the Valdrengir muster at Aldarlok. Valsal and Sólvangr empty as the honored dead draw up beside the gods for the final battle. The Asguardian telling holds that the defenders know the muster fails and gather anyway; the field gives that defiance its appointed meeting place.

entries.description: The Winter-Wolf chained at the cost of Eidgar’s hand and released at Aldarlok.
entries.note: Winter-Wolf — the wolf whose loosing is the wolf-winter
entries.prose: Vetrúlfr is the Winter-Wolf chained by Eidgar at the cost of the god’s own hand. The Faith of Eidgar reads that sacrifice as a binding whose cost falls first on the binder, and the Order of the Sworn Hand bears the broken-handed sigil in memory of it. In the standard telling of Aldarlok, Vetrúlfr slips his chain and the wolf-winter comes down. Ódvar falls to the wolf, and the wolf falls to Ódvar’s son.

entries.description: The World-Wyrm struck down by Thrúnvald in the standard telling of Aldarlok.
entries.note: World-Wyrm (Ormstead) — the Wyrm of the Crown
entries.prose: Heimsormr is the World-Wyrm in the standard Asguardian telling of Aldarlok. Thrúnvald strikes it down, walks nine steps, and dies of its venom; his priesthood reads those steps as the victory possible against a fixed doom. A separate saga gives Skalforv Thunderstrike a battle with the sea serpent, large enough to encircle the earth, whose thrashing threatens coastal villages with floods. That tale ends with Skalforv splitting its head and sending it into the depths. The hero’s saga and the telling of the god’s last battle give different encounters with the same named wyrm.

entries.description: Ódvar’s raven of thought, read both as a literal messenger and as a teaching figure.
entries.note: Thought-Friend
entries.prose: Hugvin is the raven of thought in the Faith of Ódvar, paired with Munvin, the raven of memory. The faith depicts the two flying across the world each day to gather knowledge and news for Ódvar, and reads the raven feather as their shared sign. Inside Ódvar’s rune-hall, some hold them literal, thought and memory made bird-shaped, departing at dawn and returning in the evening; ordained acolytes are taught instead that the birds are a teaching figure for the unordained, and that waiting on their reports means neglecting the work of the runes. Hnirvmýl the Wise claims to hear their whispers in the wind guiding him toward hidden knowledge and lost lore.

entries.description: Ódvar’s legendary spear, depicted as never missing its mark and signifying precision and authority.
entries.note: Shaking-Spear (Gungnir means the swaying one)
entries.prose: Skjálfgeir is the legendary spear of Ódvar. The faith depicts the god holding a weapon that never misses its mark, making it a sign of his precision and authority. A relic called Skjálfgeir’s Echo is described as a fragment of the spear and is believed to grant its bearer the same precision and authority in combat and leadership.

entries.description: Thrúnvald’s legendary hammer, a weapon of cosmic defense and a sign of protection and blessing.
entries.note: Thunder-Hammer; "the Hammer" for short
entries.prose: Thrúnhamarr is the hammer of Thrúnvald, depicted as powerful enough to crush mountains and summon thunder and lightning. The faith treats it as both the god’s weapon against the forces pressing on the ordered world and a tool of blessing and protection, joining battle and the sanctifying of ships in one symbol. The hammer stone represents that strength and protection. In the saga of Skrildmýl Stormborn, Thrumufjall is the mountain where the god is said to have struck the earth with his hammer.

entries.description: The counselor whose severed head appears beside Ódvar, associated with the well where the god pays an eye for wisdom.
entries.note: _minni_ "memory" — the Rite of Minnir's Well
entries.prose: Minnir appears in the Faith of Ódvar as a severed head from whom Ódvar continues to seek counsel. The well bearing Minnir’s name holds wisdom-bestowing waters, for a drink of which the god sacrifices an eye. Ódholm’s rune-hall tells that Ódvar seeks knowledge of the world’s end there and learns his own death at Aldarlok. Its Rite of Minnir’s Well uses a blessed chalice to stand for those waters when the rune-staves are recast for the coming season, expressing the faith’s teaching that wisdom must be paid for.

entries.description: The defending kin of the gods in archaic Asguardian liturgy, joined by common cause against Náhild and Svartbrandr.
entries.note: _Ás_ "god" (Ásgrind) + _vinir_ "friends" — the defending kin. Other forms: _Æsir_ — ash-ligature spelling; "Æsir-kin" in the import's archaic liturgies, gone from main.
entries.prose: Ásvinir is the archaic liturgical name for the defending kin of the gods. Their kinship rests on common cause against Náhild, Svartbrandr and the corruption they represent, despite the quarrels and failings of the gods themselves. It names the defending kin within the Asguardian tradition rather than every member of the Ten: Náhild and Svartbrandr belong to the broader pantheon. In the coastal tellings, the Ásvinir largely displaced the older tradition of Njörvar, whose name survives in place-names, coastal observances and the Horn of Njörvar; the sagas leave whether that elder sea-power was a god or a spirit unresolved.

entries.prose: Thrumufjall is a sheer seamount on the Nordheim coast, topped by an ancient temple of Thrúnvald and the mother-hall of the Storm-Speakers. The exposed summit serves their weather-craft training and the receptive examination held during thunderstorms. The god’s Hofgodi keeps the hof’s rites and sea-blessings beside the order, whose craft answers to different vows. In Skrildmýl Stormborn’s saga, the mountain is where Thrúnvald is said to have struck the earth with Thrúnhamarr, and the hero leads his people there through winter storms that cease after his appeal at the summit.

_mál_ "speech, sayings" (Stormmál, Málalidabandalag) + _-stead_ (Thrymstead, Lögstead, Hringstead, Ormstead) — Speech-Stead, a Malagna town

_hrand-_ "a thing set down that will not be moved" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (normalising _-stad_, with Haukstad) — the settlement's own note calls it the kingdom's "principal stronghold and de facto capital," held by one dynasty for three generations; the retired _Bjorn-_ (bear) is not a name-stem, and the note's bear-lore is kept as the Bjorn-Königer dynasty's own, not the town's

_hörgs-_ (genitive of _hörgr_, "an open stone altar"), held from a sanctuary under the theophoric clause, + _-vangr_ "an open field" — the note describes a settlement "built around a sacred grove and standing stones," an open-air altar rather than ground held for itself, so it is held from a sanctuary and not from a stem

_hvalg-_ "a bay that shelters in any wind" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Coastal Village"; a sheltering bay is the plainest sense a _-vík_ can carry for an otherwise undescribed coastal settlement

_hvarn-_ "water that will not freeze" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Coastal Village"; chosen distinct from Brúnvík/Hvalgvík so the two undescribed coastal villages are not named from the same stock, and an inlet that stays open through winter is a fact worth a village's name

_nalth-_ "the last hour of a watch" (hard grade) + _-mark_ "a march, ground held at an edge" (unchanged) — the note gives only "Border Settlement"; a frontier holding is kept by its watch, and the retired _Frost-_ is not a name-stem

_thrald-_ "the pull of a current under calm water" (hard grade) + _-fjord_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Fishing Village"; reading the fjord's current is a fisherfolk's essential skill, and the retired _Grey-_ names no stock at all

_dvarn-_ "a door that is never barred" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Port Town"; an open harbor whose door is never barred to shipping is the plainest sense a port can carry

_krald-_ "a load a beast carries without complaint" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (normalising _-stad_, per the lexicon's own arithmetic) — the note gives only "Trading Post"; a trading post lives on the pack-trains that carry its goods in

_gnaldr-_ "floes grinding on one another" (hard grade) + _-fjord_ (unchanged) — the note describes "currents that pull wrongly and lights that dance beneath the ice in winter"; the grinding of pack ice is the fjord's own defining, eerie sound, kept distinct from Ravensholm/Ódholm's Odin-held name so the two raven-adjacent settlements are not named from the same source

_vrath-_ "the temper iron takes from the fire" (hard grade) + _-havn_ (unchanged) — the note calls this Norgaad's "Iron Harbor," a militant port of smithies and a standing garrison; the tempering fire is the closest name-stem sense to the retired Iron gloss

_knarv-_ "a joint made to take strain" (hard grade) + _-vík_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Harbor Town"; chosen distinct from Járnhavn/Vrathavn (also retired an Iron- name) for the structural sense of a dock built to bear a harbor's strain, rather than the fire that tempers a blade

_hnarv-_ "the notch cut to count off a year" (hard grade) + _-dal_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Valley Settlement"; a dale is itself a notch cut into the land, echoing the stem's own sense, and the retired _Kvenn-_ opens on "kv," which Nordmal does not open on

_marv-_ "the grain in worked antler" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Town"; the stem is chosen for its plain, workaday craft sense rather than claiming a distinguishing feature the note does not state

held from a god under the theophoric clause: Ódinn's settled name _Ódvar_ (concordance, deity) clipped to its first element _ód-_, + _-holm_ (unchanged) — the note is explicit that the settlement grew up around Odin's own temple and "was founded in the age of heroes, when Odin himself walked the earth," the corpus's clearest case of a place held from a god rather than from the ground alone

_ralth-_ "how far a voice carries over water" (hard grade) + _-holm_ (normalising _-holme_, per the lexicon's own arithmetic) — the note names it only "Town"; hailing across open water is the natural sense for an otherwise undescribed holm

_gnarth-_ "the set of a jaw that will not open" (hard grade) + _-borg_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Fortified Town"; the stem's unyielding sense matches a defended stronghold where no further detail is given; Lögnheim, the crown two Malagnan polities were written as sitting under, names nothing the notes describe but the kingdom's seat, so it is folded into this row and the polities sit under the crown at Gnarthborg
_flarn-_ "a flake of stone split off by frost" (hard grade) + _-brekka_ (unchanged) — the note gives only "Mountain Settlement"; frost-shattered scree is what a slope in the high country is made of

_tvarn-_ "two things that must be counted as one" (hard grade) + _-mark_ (unchanged) — the note is explicit that the town "rises... at the confluence of two swift rivers" on the kingdom's edge, which the stem names directly and the retired _Stein-_ (stone) does not

_knalth-_ "an oath that binds without being written" (hard grade) + _-stead_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Fortified Town"; an unwritten binding oath matches a garrison town's shared defense where no further detail is given
_dvalg-_ "sleep taken standing, on watch" (hard grade) + _-heim_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Settlement"; a watchful rest suits an ordinary home where no more specific detail is given
_brald-_ "a fire banked to keep overnight" (hard grade) + _-heim_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Settlement"; a banked hearth-fire is the plainest sense a home can carry
_tvalg-_ "the lesser of a pair" (hard grade) + _-gard_ (unchanged) — the note names it only "Town"; the stem is chosen for its plainness, marking an ordinary holding rather than a distinguished one

_skrald-_ "a cry the wind carries further than it should" (hard grade) + _-borg_ (unchanged) — the note describes a "Hill Fort"; an exposed height where a warning carries unnaturally far on the wind answers the retired _Vind-_ (wind) sense while grounding it in a real name-stem

_vrild-_ (middle grade) + `-mýl` (a man) — son of Hrafnkell, so takes the grade after his father's hard; vrald 'the weight a rope will take' fits a young protector shouldering the burden of keeping others from the harm his own family suffered
_ralth-_ (hard grade) + `-thýra` (a woman) — a street-singer whose ballads move listeners in taverns and alleys; ralth 'how far a voice carries over water' is a singer's own gift
_hvalg-_ (hard grade) + `-vir` (a man) — an innkeeper whose tavern is 'a sanctuary' and 'a refuge'; hvalg 'a bay that shelters in any wind' is exactly that
_gnaldr-_ (hard grade) + `-thann` (a man) — a soldier ground down by decades of campaigns; gnaldr 'floes grinding on one another' is the friction and attrition of a life at war

entries.note: the deity's own lore article, sharing freyja's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _sól_ "sun" + _rún_ "rune" — Sun-Rune, the Gold-Bright. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the deity's own lore article, sharing freyr's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _fród-_ "peace, wisdom" + _-vin_ "friend" — Peace-Friend, the Green Lord. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the deity's own lore article, sharing hel's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _ná-_ "corpse" + _-hild_ "battle" — the Despiser of Life. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the deity's own lore article, sharing loki's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _vél_ "wile" + _grímr_ "mask" — the Wile-Mask. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the deity's own lore article, sharing odinn's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _ód-_ "fury, the seer's fit" + _-var_ "ward" — the Fury-Ward. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot. The disk shortcode oinndty is missing a letter against Ódinn; the derived newShortcode odvardty is formed correctly from Ódvar, not from the typo. Other forms: _Odin_ — bare Earth spelling with a single n; present at the import and unchanged today.

the deity's own lore article, sharing surtr's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _svart_ "black" + _brandr_ "brand, fire, blade" — the Black Brand. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the deity's own lore article, sharing thorr's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _thrún-_ "thunder" + _-vald_ "wielder". No art: the lore article carries no icon slot. Other forms: _Thór_ — bare form without the strong -r, written only as the decoration on a rank-ladder rung ("Thór Allsherjargodi", "Thor High Priest"); gone with the ladder.

the deity's own lore article, sharing tyr's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _eid_ "oath" + _-gar_ "spear" — Oath-Spear, the god sworn on at the point. No art: the lore article carries no icon slot.

the article on the Rime-Giant himself, sharing ymir's theonym with the affiliation row (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the rename touches all three independently) — see that row for the etymology: _hrím_ "rime" + _thur_ "giant" — the Rime-Giant whose body is the world. He is one of the Thursaett and not a god, so the article is filed as a spirit, which is the vocabulary's word for a supernatural being that is not divine: the shortcode's `dty` became `spr`, the file left Lore/Deities/Asguardian/ for Lore/Spirits/Asguardian/, and scope.notes names its new path so coverage still reaches it. No art: the article carries no icon slot.

entries.description: Admitted on a sworn order's own terms and dismissible on them, in three of the four Asguardian fighting orders.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: a candidate holds on the order's own terms, which is what the name has to say
entries.prose: Level 1 in three of the four Asguardian fighting orders: admitted on the order's own terms and dismissible on them.

entries.description: Instructs candidates and sits in the body that chooses its order's chair, across the four Asguardian fighting orders.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the standing is defined by instructing candidates and sitting in the body that chooses the chair. The Giant's Children call their senior the Hand of the Host, _Hershönd_ — `hers-` "a host under arms" + `-hönd` "a hand" — naming the gathered brothers he leads in the field; the order venerates the Rime-Giant, who makes nothing, so a maker's hand named something the order does not hold.
entries.prose: Level 4 across the four Asguardian fighting orders: instructs candidates and sits in the body that chooses its order's chair.

entries.description: Cast out of a sworn order, the habit taken back and the vows declared void, across the four Asguardian fighting orders.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the four orders state the condition as the act of expulsion, the habit taken back and the vows declared void
entries.prose: Level 0 across the four Asguardian fighting orders: cast out, the habit taken back and the vows declared void.

entries.description: Entrusted with the rites, the care of the faithful and the stewardship of sacred places, in the faith of Bjartr.
entries.note: a Sinalë word from the Sinalë lexicon, `ansoru` + `-nno` (one who keeps the long watch), kept with the Sinalëan structure of Bjartr's clergy; not a Nordmal coinage and not judged as one; the earlier Calathir form is retired
entries.prose: Level 3 in the faith of Bjartr: entrusted with the rites, the care of the faithful and the stewardship of sacred places.

entries.description: Those who come for the Blessing of Light and the Night of Dreams, in the faith of Bjartr.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: Bjartr's laity are named for what they come for rather than by a station word
entries.prose: Level 1 in the faith of Bjartr: those who come for the Blessing of Light and the Night of Dreams.

entries.description: Newly called to Bjartr's service, learning dream-reading, healing and the tending of groves under a Ansorunno, in the faith of Bjartr.
entries.note: a Sinalë word from the Sinalë lexicon, `ilthori` + `-nno` (a seer), kept as the faith's clergy keep the Sinalëan structure of their offices; not a Nordmal coinage and not judged as one; the earlier Tindësar form is retired
entries.prose: Level 2 in the faith of Bjartr: newly called to his service, learning dream-reading, healing and the tending of groves under a Ansorunno.

entries.description: Withheld the Aulirarno's accord, in the faith of Bjartr.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the condition is the withholding of the Aulirarno's accord, and the Sinalëan structure Bjartr's clergy keep has no Nordmal word for it
entries.prose: Level 0 in the faith of Bjartr: withheld the Aulirarno's accord.

entries.description: Attached to one of Hrímthur's scattered factions and doing its work, in the faith of Hrímthur.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, on the same pattern: the standing is attachment to a faction and the work it sets
entries.prose: Level 3 in the faith of Hrímthur: attached to one of his scattered factions and doing its work.

entries.description: Holds Hrímthur's work in awe without attaching to any faction, in the faith of Hrímthur.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: Hrímthur's scattered factions keep no priesthood and no station words, so the standing is named by the attitude that defines it
entries.prose: Level 1 in the faith of Hrímthur: holds his work in awe without attaching to any faction.

entries.description: What the cult of Náhild does to a man who gives away its hidden rites, in the faith of Náhild.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the cult names the condition by what the man did to it, and no Nordmal word is coined for a standing the cult refuses to dignify
entries.prose: Level 0 of Náhild's cult ladder: what the cult does to a man who gives away its hidden rites.

entries.description: The priest who takes Náhild's sacrifices in hiding, in the faith of Náhild.
entries.note: the kept words _godi_ and _gydja_ under the cult's possessive, both forms standing because the standing is one
entries.prose: Level 3 of Náhild's cult ladder: the priest who takes her sacrifices in hiding.

entries.description: Taught the secret observances known only to Náhild's own, in the faith of Náhild.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, on the cult ladder's possessive pattern
entries.prose: Level 2 of Náhild's cult ladder: taught the secret observances known only to her own.

entries.description: One who has turned to Náhild and brings her offering, holding none of the cult's observances, in the faith of Náhild.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, on the pattern the cult's ladder keeps throughout — each standing named by the goddess's possession of it
entries.prose: Level 1 of Náhild's cult ladder: turned to her and bringing her offering, holding none of the cult's observances.

entries.description: Declined the offering and the shared meal by a hof's godi, in the eight faiths of the Ten that keep the blót.
entries.note: the reader's tongue around the kept word _blót_: the condition is the refusal itself, so the phrase names the act rather than the person
entries.prose: Level 0 of the faith ladder in the eight faiths of the Ten that keep the blót: a hof's godi declines the offering and the shared meal, and the standing is withheld until he does not.

entries.description: One who attends the blót, the laity of the eight faiths of the Ten that keep it.
entries.note: _blót-_ "the offering and the meal that follows" + _-madr_ "a man of a station" — one who attends the blót, since a blót not attended is a blót not accomplished; the laity, level 1
entries.prose: Level 1 of the faith ladder: the laity of the eight faiths that keep the blót, whose attendance is what completes the offering.

entries.description: The ordained priest or priestess who keeps a hof's rites, in the eight faiths of the Ten that keep the blót.
entries.note: _godi_ and _gydja_ — kept words of the tongue, named among the setting's own; both forms stand in the name because the standing is one and the holder may be either
entries.prose: Level 3 of the faith ladder: the ordained priest or priestess who keeps a hof's rites.

entries.description: The high priest who consecrates a hof and performs the great blót at a season's turning, in the eight faiths of the Ten that keep it.
entries.note: _hof-_ "the temple building" + the kept _godi_ / _gydja_ — keeper of a named hof; both forms stand in the name because the standing is one
entries.prose: Level 4 of the faith ladder: consecrates a hof and performs the great blót at a season's turning.

entries.description: The sovereign standing of the Jarldom of Stormveld, held by a jarl elected from among his peers.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, built on the kept word _jarl_: Stormveld seats no king, so its sovereign standing is a jarl raised above jarls rather than a crown
entries.prose: The sovereign standing of the Jarldom of Stormveld, held by a jarl elected from among his peers rather than by a royal clan's acclamation.

entries.description: Full clan membership, holding odal land and a voice at the ting, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _bóndi_ — a kept word of the tongue for the odal-holding freeman; level 3, where the ting enfranchises the commons, and the word stands rather than drifting
entries.prose: Level 3 of the civic ladder, the full clan member: holds his own odal land by inheritance, bears arms, and speaks at the ting in a ruling that binds the jarl over him.

entries.description: The nobility, holding a province of the king and commanding its hersvaldar, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _jarl_ — a kept word of the tongue, named among the setting's own; level 6, the nobility holding a province of the king
entries.prose: Level 6 of the civic ladder: holds a province by the king's grant, commands its hersvaldar, and answers to the king for its peace — a grant the crown can move, unlike a bóndi's odal land.

entries.description: The sovereign, chosen from the royal clans and acclaimed at the ting, in the five kingdoms.
entries.note: the standing is written in the reader's tongue, as the Lawspeaker and the Queen are; the Nordmal _konungr_ stands behind the shortcode, and the faith ladder's own Konungr is retired, so the word is left to the polity alone
entries.prose: Level 7 of the civic ladder: chosen from the royal clans and acclaimed at the ting, holding the realm on the assembly's continuing consent, which can refuse to hand his arm-ring back.

entries.description: Outlawed at the ting and set beyond the law's protection, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _níding_ — the north's own word for a man set outside the law, named in the tongue's kept words; the ladder's level 0, cast out, and the word stands rather than drifting
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Nordmal civic ladder in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld: outlawed at the ting, killing him draws no penalty, and a hall that shelters him answers for it.

entries.description: Owned outright, owing labor rather than rent and holding no voice at the ting, in the five kingdoms and the Jarldom of Stormveld.
entries.note: _thrall_ — a kept word of the tongue, the man owned outright; level 1, the lowest standing the law still describes, and unfreedom is a rank because the law treats him apart
entries.prose: Level 1 of the civic ladder: owned rather than born free, owing labour itself rather than rent, barred from arms and unheard at the ting.

entries.description: A common warrior of a Compact-signed company, testified by his captain, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the standing is the oath a captain testifies to, so the name says sworn and says of what
entries.prose: Level 1 of Málalidabandalag: a common warrior of a Compact-signed company, testified by his captain.

entries.description: Expelled from the Compact by Council vote, the bronze thumb-ring surrendered, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the Compact states the condition as the discharge and the surrender of the bronze thumb-ring
entries.prose: Level 0 of Málalidabandalag: expelled from the Compact by Council vote, the bronze thumb-ring surrendered.

entries.description: Swears the Compact before the Council of the Hall and wears the bandalagshringr, in Málalidabandalag.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: signing the Compact before the Council is the act that confers the standing, and the bandalagshringr is its mark
entries.prose: Level 3 of Málalidabandalag: swears the Compact before the Council of the Hall and wears the bandalagshringr.

entries.description: The full member of the Order of the Giant's Children, admitted by a rite of ordeal and theological examination.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from Thursbörn's own theology: the full member is born of the founding wound, admitted by ordeal and examination
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Giant's Children: the full member, admitted by a rite of ordeal and theological examination.

entries.description: The working warden of the Order of the Green Wardens, holding a station or riding circuit relief.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: Grönverdir's working member is a sworn guardian
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Green Wardens: the working warden, holding a station or riding circuit relief.

entries.description: The full member of the Order of the Storm-Speakers, acting on the order's behalf across the Nordlands.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: a Storm-Speaker's full member is a sworn speaker
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Storm-Speakers: acts on the order's behalf across the Nordlands.

entries.description: The warrior-judge of the Order of the Sworn Hand, riding circuit to render and enforce rulings under the white wand.
entries.note: the reader's tongue, from the order's own name: Eidhönd's full member is a sworn hand, and the order's title carries the Nordmal form
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Order of the Sworn Hand: the warrior-judge who rides circuit to render and enforce rulings under the white wand.

entries.description: Convicted of breaking the truth of the recital, the arm-ring broken at the next Skaldating, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: the reader's tongue around the ring the Circle gives: the condition is named by the breaking, which is what the Skaldating does
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Skalds' Circle: convicted of breaking the truth of the recital, the arm-ring broken at the next Skaldating.

entries.description: Acclaimed by his peers when his composed sagas enter the standing repertoire, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: _stórald_ "the great telling" + _-stjóri_ "one who directs a thing" — the master whose composed sagas enter the standing repertoire
entries.prose: Level 4 of the Skalds' Circle: acclaimed by his peers when his composed sagas enter the standing repertoire.

entries.description: Sworn keeper of a hall's record, entitled to food, shelter and safe passage at any hall, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: _skald_ — a kept word of the tongue, named among the setting's own; the sworn keeper of a hall's record
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Skalds' Circle: sworn keeper of a hall's record, entitled to food, shelter and safe passage at any hall.

entries.description: A master's pupil for ten to fifteen years, entitled to present a gyldra, in the Skalds' Circle.
entries.note: the reader's tongue: the standing is a pupillage of ten to fifteen years, and the Circle names it plainly
entries.prose: Level 1 of the Skalds' Circle: a master's pupil for ten to fifteen years, entitled to present a gyldra.

entries.description: One of the six who follow Dágulf Véthar, held by fear of the leader and the absence of better options, in the Blackpine Wolves.
entries.note: _grim-_ (fierce, the war-mask that hides a face) + `-mund` (the one who holds a thing safe) — held fast by the fierce one's hand, which is the whole of the standing.
entries.prose: The single standing of the Blackpine Wolves: one of the six who follow Dágulf Véthar, held by fear of the leader and the absence of better options.

entries.description: Taken in war or bought at the river-landings, answering to the mistress of a household about everything, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _óth-_ (a kindred's holding, what passes to an heir) + `-mund` (the one who holds a thing safe) — held as part of a household's holding, bought, worked and watched.
entries.prose: Level 1 of the Vrystwald Tribes: taken in war or bought at the river-landings, answering to the mistress of a household about everything.

entries.description: Cast out by their own kin and claimed by none, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _vryst-_ (free, held by nobody) + `-rith` (the one who rides a ground) — one who rides unclaimed, claimed by no kindred's bound.
entries.prose: Level 0 of the Vrystwald Tribes: cast out by their own kin and claimed by none.

entries.description: Of a kindred's blood, entitled to its protection, its feud and its share, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _druth-_ (what is trusted) + `-mund` (the one who holds a thing safe) — the trusted one, held safe by his kindred's blood.
entries.prose: Level 3 of the Vrystwald Tribes: of a kindred's blood, entitled to its protection, its feud and its share.

entries.description: Holds one of the three seats that govern a village together, so that the village's vote never ties, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _fród-_ (wise, seasoned by years) + `-rád` (the one who counsels on a thing) — the wise one who sits in one of the village's three seats.
entries.prose: Level 5 of the Vrystwald Tribes: holds one of the three seats that govern a village together, so that the village's vote never ties.

entries.description: Bears a charge on the renown a deed has already won, assisting the elders in everyday duties, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _hród-_ (renown) + `-thúl` (one who endures and bears a charge) — the one who bears a charge on their renown.
entries.prose: Level 4 of the Vrystwald Tribes: bears a charge on the renown a deed has already won, assisting the elders in everyday duties.

entries.description: Free and of no kin, sheltered by a household without being of its blood, in the Vrystwald Tribes.
entries.note: _edr-_ (a hedge, the bound set about a holding) + `-mund` (the one who holds a thing safe) — kept safe within another household's hedge without being of its blood.
entries.prose: Level 2 of the Vrystwald Tribes: free and of no kin, sheltered by a household without being of its blood.

entries.description: One of the company, carrying a charge and a share of the kill, in Wuldjagár erund Gárskald.
entries.note: _erth-_ (the earth, the ground underfoot) + `-jagár` (the one who hunts a ground) — hunts the clan's ground and carries a charge on it.
entries.prose: Level 3 of Wuldjagár erund Gárskald: one of the company, carrying a charge and a share of the kill.

entries.description: Recently inducted and still learning the ways, watched for signs of weakness, in Wuldjagár erund Gárskald.
entries.note: _vand-_ (exacting, hard to satisfy) + `-ár` (the one who answers for a thing) — watched by exacting eyes until trusted further.
entries.prose: Level 1 of Wuldjagár erund Gárskald: recently inducted and still learning the ways, watched for signs of weakness.

entries.note: eth spelling of the Compact's own name, used throughout the import; the name itself stands and is on the keep-list, so only the spelling moves — the romanisation rule writes a plain d where the import wrote an eth. The note's shortcode and address are unaffected, and both halves state so.

entries.description: Elder-trained fighters of Bjartr's will.
entries.note: the bright blade, from `bjart-` (bright) and `-brandr` (a brand, either a firebrand or a blade). Eldingsekr was built from `elding-` and `-sekr`, neither of which the element lexicon publishes, so the compound rule refused it; the lawful coinage says the same thing from published stock, and the English phrase the faith note glossed it with is kept as the alias: the one body in Bjartr's service built for battle, carrying the elder races' training as a blade of his light.

entries.description: The rare standing between the elder races and mortals.
entries.note: the age's voice, from `aldar-` (an age's) and `-mál` (speech, and the voice a body speaks with). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Bjartr's faith note kept as its alias: the standing speaks between the elder races and mortals, so the name is the voice the elder age speaks with.

entries.description: Healing and counsel in Bjartr's light.
entries.note: the bright hand, from `bjart-` (bright) and `-hönd` (a hand). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Bjartr's faith note kept as its alias: healers and counselors who tend a wound and a troubled dream as one care, so the hand that carries Bjartr's light.

entries.description: Warriors sworn to Eidgar's heaviest oaths.
entries.note: the oath-wards, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: warriors under oaths heavier than a soldier's, sworn to the defense of the faith and the hofs where its tings sit.

entries.description: Witnesses and mediators of Eidgar's sworn oaths.
entries.note: the oath-ring, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-ringr` (a ring, and a circle of sworn men). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: priests who witness an oath and keep its memory, a circle of sworn men answering to neither side of a quarrel.

entries.description: Combat and justice at Eidgar's hofs.
entries.note: the law's blade, from `lög-` (the law as it is recited) and `-brandr` (a brand, either a firebrand or a blade). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: priests who hear a dispute at the hof where the ting sits and draw the blade that enforces the ruling.

entries.description: Eidgar's fighting order of honorable combat.
entries.note: the oath-champions, from `eid-` (an oath sworn at a spear-point) and `-káppar` (champions). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Eidgar's faith note kept as its alias: the faith's elite fighting order, the arm a ting's ruling calls on when it needs one.

entries.description: Body and soul tended at Fródvin's infirmaries.
entries.note: the hall's friends, from `hallar-` (a great hall's) and `-vinir` (friends). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: indoor and constant work at the valley infirmaries, the sick tended and the distressed comforted as a household's own would be.

entries.description: Mediation and harmony in Fródvin's name.
entries.note: the peace-bearer, from `fród-` (the peace that wisdom buys) and `-beri` (one who bears a thing). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: mediators who carry Fródvin's peace into a quarrel before it reaches the ting.

entries.description: Herb-lore and healing in Fródvin's service.
entries.note: the green hand, from `grön-` (green, and growing) and `-hönd` (a hand). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Fródvin's faith note kept as its alias: herbalists who keep the sacred groves and the herb-lore Fródvin's healing depends on.

entries.description: Náhild's doctrine spread through fear.
entries.note: the corpse-speakers, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-maelendir` (ones that speak). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: they carry Náhild's doctrine beyond her hidden hofs by speaking it where a public blót could never reach.

entries.description: Guardians and inquisitors of Náhild's hidden hofs.
entries.note: the corpse-wards, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-verdir` (wards, keepers). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: the cult's own inquisitors, guarding her hidden hofs and the rites kept inside them.

entries.description: Náhild's elite assassins.
entries.note: the night-goers, from `nótt-` (night) and `-gengir` (ones that go). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: her assassins, whose killings are chosen for the fear they spread as much as for the target.

entries.description: Náhild's hidden cult of the Eye of the Void.
entries.note: the corpse-end, from `ná-` (a corpse) and `-lok` (a close, an end). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias: the hidden cult of the ending, widening the Eye of the Void's reach where no outsider can see the work.

entries.description: The Eye of the Void: Náhild's primordial relic of corruption, worn at her neck and a powerful source of the Shadow.
entries.note: _ginn-_ "the yawning void beyond creation" + _-auga_ "an eye" — the Eye of the Void. The relic's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Náhild's faith note kept as its alias and in the prose.
entries.prose: Ginnauga, the Eye of the Void, is the primordial relic from which Náhild draws her power. It is a powerful source of the Shadow, the chaos from outside creation that corrupts whatever it touches, mortal or divine, and that is what makes the Eye so terrible. Its influence corrupts everything near it, and a caustic shadow of dread and hopelessness seeps from it into the mortal world.

entries.description: The pursuit and keeping of Ódvar's knowledge.
entries.note: the kin of thought, from `hug-` (thought) and `-aett` (a kin reckoned together). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Ódvar's faith note kept as its alias: the most learned of Ódvar's faithful, reckoned together as one body and keeping the libraries at its temples.

entries.description: Rune-lore and divination in Ódvar's service.
entries.note: the raven-rune, from `hrafn-` (a raven) and `-rún` (a rune). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Ódvar's faith note kept as its alias: rune-lore and divination, the staves cast for warbands, jarls and households who need counsel a blót does not supply.

entries.description: Diplomacy and persuasion for Sólrún's faith.
entries.note: the gold-speech, from `gull-` (gold) and `-mál` (speech, and the voice a body speaks with). The order's own name in Nordmal, with the English phrase it answered to in Sólrún's faith note kept as its alias: the voice Sólrún's faith speaks with in dealings no blunter envoy could carry.

entries.description: Put out of a devotional order of the faiths of the Ten, forfeiting its shelter and its purpose alike.
entries.note: the sworn band's outlaw, from `drótt-` (a war-band sworn to one man) and `-vargr` (an outlaw, a wolf in the law's eye). The three standings every one of the twenty-nine shares are built on one element, so the ladder reads as one, as Grönvördr and Eldri Grönvördr do. A closing that names what a member has become is not an office suffix by § _Ranks, offices and orders_, which is why this one is a plain compound where the other two take office suffixes — the same shape Sárborinn carries. The two single-word aliases go: an alias is an English phrase that says what a thing is.

entries.description: The giant-kin defeated by the Ten, with Hrímthur killed and the rest banished to Thursguard.
entries.prose: Thursaett names the giant-kin the Ten fought before the world stood. In the Asguardian account, the gods defeated them and drove the surviving kin into Thursguard, a plane of their own. Hrímthur alone was killed rather than banished, and the Ten cut Mannguard from his body. The tradition gives the giant-kin their place on the defeated side of that founding war without describing their life inside the plane that confines them.
entries.note: `thurs-` "a giant" + `-aett` "a kin reckoned together" — built to stand against Ásvinir, the defending kin, which is the same shape: a kin-word for the gods' side wants a kin-word for the side they beat. The English word is "giant", which the corpus already writes for Hrímthur and for the Giant's Children; a Greek term for the class would be the same borrowing as Aesir, which this programme retires.

entries.description: The plane that confines the giant-kin defeated by the Ten.
entries.prose: Thursguard is the plane into which the Ten drove the defeated Thursaett before the world stood. Hrímthur alone was killed instead, his body cut into Mannguard. The Asguardian teaching distinguishes Thursguard from Mannguard and Asguard, the two worlds joined by Heimsask. No telling describes Thursguard from within; the rune-priests teach only that the giant-kin are confined there and that nothing has come back out.
entries.note: `thurs-` "a giant" + `-guard` "an enclosed world" — the third name on the pattern Asguard and Mannguard already set, and built from the same published closing element so a reader who knows those two reads this one on sight.

entries.description: The Maker of the Asguardian gods—craft, invention, and the made creatures that cannot breed.
entries.prose: The tenth god of the Ten and the one whose work can be met on a road: he invents, he makes each living thing once, he releases much of it unfinished, and he does not come back for it. The Dreadspawn are his. Where he works is unknown, and his hofs hold several irreconcilable accounts of vast laboratories.
entries.note: `mót-` "a shape, a mould" + `-efnir` "one in the making" — the shaper ever in the making. `-efnir` is the only published closing element that carries incompleteness, which is what the god needs: his creatures go out unfinished, so the name says of him what he does to them. The maker conception the corpus already held had no name of its own and travelled under the retired theonym the Rime-Giant's row records; it is his, and only the conception was carried, never a name — so there is no old half here. `mót-` is published in the opening elements by the same change that writes this row.

entries.description: Craft, Invention and the Made.
entries.prose: The faith kept almost entirely by people who make things for a living, on the ordinary blót ladder every public faith of the Ten keeps. Its offering is work rather than cattle: a craftsman swears his first work at a hof and it stays on the shelf behind the altar, and a man who knowingly sells bad work is refused the blót.
entries.note: the faith note, sharing the god's bare shortcode with its ritual skill (a shortcode is unique only within one type, so the two notes carry the name independently) — see the deity row for the etymology. Its alias is an English phrase on the pattern every other faith of the Ten uses, and names what the god does to his work rather than what he is. No art: the icon slot is unfilled, because the nine painted faith icons are drawn art and none exists for this faith yet.

entries.prose: The faith skill, which points at the faith note and carries nothing of its own beyond the mastery formula every faith skill of the Ten shares.

entries.description: The seasonal return of ships, warriors and cattle, with offerings and great assemblies.
entries.note: Kept seasonal folk word published in Nordmal’s four turns of the year; context from the Asguardian calendar and Nordheimn customs.
entries.prose: Sumarmál is the seasonal blót of return: ships go back to the water, warriors leave winter quarters, and cattle go to pasture. Offerings seek a good growing and sailing year, with Fródvin prominent and Thrúnvald invoked for seafaring. Great tings hear disputes and witness public oaths. On the frontier, neighboring householders may walk their boundary stones with a witness for the landvördr, reading and striking each mark; a moved stone becomes a matter for the ting.

entries.description: The Winter Nights of late autumn, when households prepare for scarcity and honor the dead.
entries.note: Kept seasonal folk word published in Nordmal’s four turns of the year; context from the Asguardian calendar and Nordheimn customs.
entries.prose: Vetrnaetr, the Winter Nights, marks the late-autumn turn toward winter. Livestock that cannot be kept through the scarcity are slaughtered in a great blót, meat is preserved, bones are read, and the dead are honored. Sólrún receives the greatest portion and Ódvar is invoked for the coming long dark. A hall’s búvördr seats its honored elders by the door and serves them first; a household unable to provision them must seek help from other kin and halls. The season also permits the howe-wake under a völva’s customary leave, without giving private revelation the authority of living evidence or a ting judgment.

entries.description: The north's howe-wardens: Náhild's mindless raised dead, and the dead said to keep their own mounds.
entries.note: howe-wardens, a common noun: _hrúm-_ "a howe" + `-verdir` "wardens". Other forms: _haugbúar_ — lower-case form; _Haugbúi_ — singular of Haugbúar, written out rather than matched through an inflection; _Haugverdir_ and _haugverdir_ — built on _haug-_, the Old Norse word for a howe, which the Norse review recoined as _hrúm-_.
entries.prose: Hrúmverdir, the howe-wardens, is a northern word for undead put to two uses. Both name a body that moves after death, and both name something touched by the Shadow, which binds every undead to every other across every belief and culture. The two uses keep their own meanings, and the word does not make one of the other.

entries.description: The twelve nights of midwinter feasts, vigil and remembrance.
entries.note: Kept seasonal folk word published in Nordmal’s four turns of the year; context from the Asguardian calendar and Nordheimn customs. The Kingdom of Nordheim's midwinter _Jólblót_ is this festival; the name is retired.
entries.prose: Jól is the twelve-night midwinter season around the solstice, when hofs keep their lights burning and halls open their feasts. The dead are invited to the table, and the living keep vigil against the long dark. Ódvar is prominent in the season; Thrúnvald’s priests bless the hearth, Sólrún’s priestesses conduct rites for loves and marriages, and skalds sing the cycle of hero-sagas. A seeker may keep the howe-wake on its ninth night, with a völva’s customary leave, but a private answer from the dead must be supported by living evidence.

entries.description: The summer-solstice festival of coastal bonfires, shared feasts and light.
entries.note: Kept seasonal folk word published in Nordmal’s four turns of the year; context from the Asguardian calendar and Nordheimn customs. The Kingdom of Nordheim's midsummer _Sigrblót_ is this festival, not a fifth one; the name is retired.
entries.prose: Midsumar is the summer-solstice festival, when the sun barely sets and the northern coasts kindle bonfires on their promontories. Shared feasts celebrate light and community, with Bjartr central to the observance. The faithful leap low flames for luck, and the long bonfire-night brings the community together at the brightest turn of the year.
